deck.title: Classic Traps & Must-Know Combos
deck.analogy: This section is the map of the minefield: every trap is a wrong answer that sounds right, paired with the truth that defuses it.

subtopics.title: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: What is the SAA-C03 really testing, per the exam traps guide?

back.answer: Whether you know where the tripwires are: wrong answers that sound right, paired with the truth that defuses them.
back.explanation: Walk the trap list twice before exam day.

cards.front: Trap: read from the RDS Multi-AZ standby to offload queries. True?

back.answer: No. The standby is invisible; use read replicas for reads.

cards.front: Trap: Route 53 CNAME record at the zone apex (example.com). Valid?

back.answer: No. CNAMEs can't sit at the apex; use an Alias record.

cards.front: Trap: add a deny rule to the EC2 security group. Possible?

back.answer: No. Security groups are allow-only and stateful; deny rules live in NACLs.

cards.front: Trap: private subnet reaches S3 via NAT Gateway. Best answer?

back.answer: It works but costs money; a Gateway VPC Endpoint is free and private.

cards.front: Trap: run a 20-minute job in Lambda. Valid?

back.answer: No. Lambda caps at 15 minutes; use Fargate, Batch, or Step Functions.

cards.front: Trap: mount EFS on Windows instances. Valid?

back.answer: No. EFS is Linux-only; Windows shared storage is FSx for Windows File Server.

cards.front: Trap: Snowball imports directly into Glacier. True?

back.answer: No. Snowball lands in S3; a lifecycle policy then moves data to Glacier.

cards.front: Trap: VPC peering A↔B and B↔C lets A reach C. True?

back.answer: No. Peering is non-transitive; use Transit Gateway or direct A↔C peering.

cards.front: Trap: encrypt an existing unencrypted RDS/EBS in place. Possible?

back.answer: No. Snapshot, copy the snapshot with encryption, then restore.

cards.front: Trap: use KMS for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or single-tenant keys. Correct?

back.answer: No. That's CloudHSM; KMS is Level 2 and multi-tenant.

cards.front: Trap: Shield Standard stops layer-7 application attacks. True?

back.answer: No. Standard covers L3/L4 only; L7 protection is WAF or Shield Advanced.

cards.front: Trap: apply an SCP to restrict the AWS Organizations management account. Works?

back.answer: No. SCPs never affect the management account.

cards.front: Trap: replay DynamoDB Streams data from last month. Possible?

back.answer: No. Streams keep 24 hours; longer retention needs Kinesis Data Streams.

cards.front: Trap: give the ALB a static IP. Possible?

back.answer: No. ALBs have no static IPs; NLB has static/Elastic IPs (or put NLB in front of ALB).

cards.front: Trap: add an LSI to an existing DynamoDB table. Possible?

back.answer: No. LSIs only at table creation; afterwards add a GSI.

cards.front: Trap: accelerate UDP traffic with CloudFront. Valid?

back.answer: No. CloudFront is HTTP(S) only; TCP/UDP acceleration is Global Accelerator.

cards.front: Trap: Systems Manager Parameter Store rotates the DB password automatically. True?

back.answer: No native rotation; automatic rotation is Secrets Manager.

cards.front: Trap: one NAT Gateway serves all AZs and is highly available. True?

back.answer: No. An AZ failure kills it; deploy one NAT Gateway per AZ.

cards.front: Trap: SNS alone guarantees consumers never miss messages. True?

back.answer: No. SNS doesn't persist for offline consumers; durable fan-out is SNS → SQS.

cards.front: Trap: Direct Connect is encrypted because it's private. True?

back.answer: No. It's not encrypted; run a VPN over DX for encryption.

cards.front: Which AWS services form the serverless web app combo?

back.answer: CloudFront + S3 (static) + API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB.

cards.sourceHeading: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: Which combo gives reliable fan-out on AWS?

back.answer: SNS → multiple SQS queues; durable, each consumer has its own queue.

cards.sourceHeading: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: Which services give a global highly available database (SQL vs NoSQL)?

back.answer: Aurora Global Database (SQL); DynamoDB Global Tables (NoSQL).

cards.sourceHeading: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: Which combo protects a web app on AWS?

back.answer: CloudFront + WAF + Shield + ALB.

cards.sourceHeading: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: Which combo builds a real-time streaming pipeline?

back.answer: Kinesis Data Streams → Lambda → DynamoDB/S3.

cards.sourceHeading: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: Which services combine for analytics on a data lake, and what does each do?

back.answer: S3 + Glue (catalog/ETL) + Athena (query) + QuickSight (dashboards).

cards.sourceHeading: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: What is the AWS migration toolkit combo?

back.answer: DataSync (files) + DMS (databases) + DX/Snow family (transport).

cards.sourceHeading: Must-know combos (the exam's favorite Lego sets)

cards.front: What is the DR stack combo on AWS?

back.answer: Route 53 failover + Aurora Global + S3 CRR.

cards.front: Cognito User Pools vs Identity Pools in app authentication?

back.answer: User Pools handle login; Identity Pools hand out AWS credentials.

cards.front: Exam technique: which part of an SAA-C03 question should you read first?

back.answer: The last sentence; it holds the actual question and qualifier.
back.explanation: The story above it is scenery.

cards.front: Exam technique: how do you narrow the answers?

back.answer: Eliminate the two obviously wrong answers, then compare the survivors.

cards.front: How do exam qualifiers decide between two working answers?

back.answer: Cost → cheapest that works; least overhead → most managed/serverless; HA → Multi-AZ; region failure → multi-region.

cards.front: SAA-C03 pacing: how long per question, and what if stuck?

back.answer: About 2 minutes each (130 min, 65 questions); if stuck at 90 seconds, flag and move on.

cards.front: Is there a penalty for wrong answers on the SAA-C03?

back.answer: No. Answer everything; a guess beats a blank.

cards.front: Route example.com (apex) to an ALB. What do you use in Route 53?

back.answer: Alias record.
back.explanation: CNAME is illegal at the apex.

choices.why: Alias works at apex and targets ALB.

cards.front: Block a specific malicious IP address in a VPC. What do you use?

back.answer: NACL deny rule.

choices.why: Security groups have no deny rules.

cards.front: A private subnet needs S3 access at no cost. What do you use?

back.answer: Gateway VPC Endpoint.
back.explanation: NAT Gateway is the paid decoy.

cards.front: How do you encrypt an existing unencrypted RDS instance?

back.answer: Snapshot → encrypted copy → restore.

choices.text: Create a read replica with encryption

cards.front: Fan out orders to inventory, billing, shipping; none may be lost. What design?

back.answer: SNS topic → three SQS queues.

choices.why: Each consumer gets a durable queue.

choices.text: SNS topic with three subscribers only

cards.front: The firewall team requires static IPs for the load balancer. What do you use?

back.answer: Network Load Balancer.

choices.why: DNS doesn't give load balancer static IPs.

cards.front: Improve performance AND get static IPs for a global TCP/UDP app. What do you use?

back.answer: Global Accelerator.

cards.front: Rotate database credentials automatically every 30 days. What do you use?

back.answer: Secrets Manager.

back.answer: NACL (never SG)

back.answer: Gateway Endpoint

cards.front: Keyword: **">15 minutes"**

back.answer: Not Lambda (Fargate/Batch)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Windows file share"**

back.answer: FSx for Windows

cards.front: Keyword: **"Transitive routing"**

back.answer: Transit Gateway

cards.front: Keyword: **"Encrypt existing volume/DB"**

back.answer: Snapshot dance

cards.front: Keyword: **"FIPS Level 3"**

back.answer: CloudHSM

cards.front: Keyword: **"Static IP load balancer"**

back.answer: NLB

cards.front: Keyword: **"UDP acceleration"**

back.answer: Global Accelerator

cards.front: Keyword: **"Auto-rotation"**

back.answer: Secrets Manager

cards.front: Keyword: **"HA NAT"**

back.answer: One per AZ

cards.front: Keyword: **"Durable fan-out"**

back.answer: SNS → SQS

cards.front: Keyword: **"Encrypted DX"**

back.answer: VPN over DX
